 AI Assistant WebMCP — Project Story 

 Inspiration 

 Small clinics, counseling centers, and SMBs have websites, but no AI to answer the basic questions visitors ask around the clock — booking, pricing, location. General-purpose chatbots don't know the business's actual information and end up hallucinating. We wanted to give every small business an AI assistant that actually knows their site, without requiring any engineering effort from them. 

 What it does 

 WebMCP is a fully automated AI-assistant SaaS. You paste a URL, and it: 

 
 Crawls the site (sitemap-based, multi-page) 
 Generates industry-specific Q&A with an LLM 
 Builds a widget (5 themes, voice input, quick-menu) 
 Ships a paste-and-go embed ( /embed/<id>.js ) 
 

 Visitors then chat with an AI that answers from the site's real knowledge — with off-topic screening and hallucination guards built in. 

 How we built it 

 
 Nuxt 3 (SSR) console + Django 5/DRF backend + vanilla JS widget (single loader embed) 
 Celery-free polling worker — select_for_update + lock-expiry auto-recovery for restart resilience 
 Dual LLM engines — Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite for real-time chat (low latency + off-topic guard), OpenRouter gpt-oss-120b for batch Q&A (~$0.00196/run) 
 Multilingual silos — ko/en fully separated across DB, containers, prompts, and UI 
 3-stage deployment — Docker Compose → self-hosted server (nginx + Let's Encrypt) → Render Blueprint (IaC) 
 

 Challenges we ran into 

 
 Passive → proactive AI — the ideal is the widget JS dynamically scanning and injecting into site forms (no owner-side changes), but form structures vary wildly. We deliberately deferred form control and focused on chat automation. 
 Crawling engine trade-off — plain HTTP parsers fail on WAF/SPA sites; browser crawlers are too heavy. Solved with a dual engine (httpx + browser-header fallback). 
 Off-topic questions — solved with system-prompt bounding + cached Q&A similarity matching (≥0.6), verified stable on Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite. 
 Multi-tenant security — Origin allowlist + publicId auth, per-tenant keys, global IP-allowlist switch. 
 Platform quirks — Render misread a dockerCommand chain as a filename, crashing the worker in a loop. 
 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of 

 
 End-to-end automation — URL in, working widget out, validated all the way to the cloud. 
 Cost engineering — batch Q&A at ~$0.00196/run using OSS models, with similarity caching to cut expensive calls. 
 Structural multilingualism — language mixing blocked at the architecture level, not via translation keys. 
 45 documented test records (T-001~T-045) and a troubleshooting FAQ that prevent repeat mistakes. 
 

 What we learned 

 
 Scope selection is the essence of automation — one feature done end-to-end beats many half-done features. 
 Combine models by purpose — cost-effective OSS for batch, low-latency Gemini for real-time. 
 The prompt is a security layer — off-topic filtering via prompt bounding, at zero extra cost. 
 Security should be a switch, not a default — environment-adaptable controls are what make them practical. 
 

 What's next for AI assistant WebMCP 

 
 Proactive form integration — the widget JS dynamically scanning and injecting into site forms (booking, contact), so the AI can complete actions, not just answer. 
 Broader language silos — Japanese, Chinese, and more, following the existing 4-step extension path. 
 Deeper model routing — per-tenant model selection and cost controls at scale. 
 

 

 AI 어시스턴트 WebMCP — 프로젝트 스토리 

 Inspiration (영감) 

 소규모 병원·상담센터·중소기업은 웹사이트는 있지만, 방문자가 24시간 궁금해하는 기본 질문(예약, 요금, 위치)에 답해줄 AI가 없습니다. 범용 챗봇은 그 업체의 실제 정보를 몰라 환각을 일으킵니다. 우리는 엔지니어링 노력 없이도 모든 소규모 사업체가 자기 사이트를 진짜 아는 AI 비서를 가질 수 있게 하고 싶었습니다. 

 What it does (하는 일) 

 WebMCP는 완전 자동화 AI 비서 SaaS입니다. URL만 붙여넣으면: 

 
 크롤링 (sitemap 기반 멀티페이지) 
 업종별 Q&A 생성 (LLM) 
 위젯 빌드 (5종 테마, 음성 입력, 빠른메뉴) 
 붙여넣기 임베드 배포 ( /embed/<id>.js ) 
 

 방문자는 사이트의 실제 지식을 바탕으로 답하는 AI와 대화합니다 — 오프토픽 스크리닝과 환각 방지 가드가 내장되어 있습니다. 

 How we built it (구축 방법) 

 
 Nuxt 3(SSR) 콘솔 + Django 5/DRF 백엔드 + vanilla JS 위젯 (단일 로더 임베드) 
 Celery 없는 폴링 워커 — select_for_update + 잠금 만료 자동 복구로 재시작 내성 확보 
 LLM 이중 엔진 — 실시간 채팅은 Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite(저지연+오프토픽 가드), 배치 Q&A는 OpenRouter gpt-oss-120b (1회 약 $0.00196) 
 다국어 사일로 — ko/en을 DB·컨테이너·프롬프트·UI까지 완전 분리 
 3단계 배포 — Docker Compose → 자체 서버(nginx+Let's Encrypt) → Render Blueprint(IaC) 
 

 Challenges we ran into (직면한 도전) 

 
 수동적 → 능동적 AI — 이상은 위젯 JS가 사이트 폼을 동적으로 스캔·삽입하는 것(소유자 수정 불필요)이지만, 폼 구조가 천차만별이라 의도적으로 폼 제어를 미루고 채팅 자동화에 집중했습니다. 
 크롤링 엔진 트레이드오프 — 단순 HTTP 파서는 WAF/SPA를 못 읽고, 브라우저 크롤러는 너무 무거움. 이중 엔진(httpx + 브라우저 헤더 폴백)으로 해결. 
 오프토픽 질문 — 시스템 프롬프트 바운딩 + 저장 Q&A 유사도 매칭(≥0.6)으로 해결, Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite에서 안정 동작 확인. 
 멀티테넌트 보안 — Origin 화이트리스트 + publicId 인증, 테넌트별 키, 전역 IP 화이트리스트 스위치. 
 플랫폼 특이점 — Render가 dockerCommand 체인을 파일명으로 오판해 워커가 크래시 루프에 빠짐. 
 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of (자랑스러운 성과) 

 
 엔드투엔드 자동화 — URL 입력 → 동작하는 위젯 출력, 클라우드까지 검증 완료. 
 비용 엔지니어링 — OSS 모델로 배치 Q&A 1회 약 $0.00196, 유사도 캐시로 고비용 호출 절감. 
 구조적 다국어 — 번역 키가 아닌 아키텍처 레벨에서 언어 혼용 차단. 
 45건의 테스트 기록 (T-001~T-045)과 트러블슈팅 FAQ로 재발 방지. 
 

 What we learned (배운 점) 

 
 자동화의 본질은 범위 선택 — 하나를 끝까지 완성하는 것이 여러 개를 반쯤 하는 것보다 낫습니다. 
 모델은 용도별 조합 — 배치는 가성비 OSS, 실시간은 저지연 Gemini. 
 프롬프트가 보안 계층 — 오프토픽 필터링을 프롬프트 바운딩으로, 추가 비용 없이 해결. 
 보안은 스위치로 설계 — 환경에 맞게 조절 가능해야 실용적입니다. 
 

 What's next for AI assistant WebMCP (다음 단계) 

 
 능동적 폼 통합 — 위젯 JS가 사이트 폼(예약·문의)을 동적으로 스캔·삽입해, AI가 답변을 넘어 행동을 완수 하도록. 
 더 넓은 언어 사일로 — 일본어·중국어 등, 기존 4단계 확장 경로를 따라 추가. 
 고도화된 모델 라우팅 — 테넌트별 모델 선택과 대규모 비용 통제.

 Project Name: AI QR Studio (WebMCP Enabled)
Project Tagline: A smart, agent-friendly QR & Barcode generator that bridges natural language UI with the WebMCP protocol for seamless AI automation. 

 
 About the Project:
AI QR Studio is a modern, single-page web application designed to solve two core problems: simplifying complex QR/Barcode creation for everyday users through natural language, and exposing tool capabilities to autonomous AI agents via the WebMCP standard. Users can type requests like "Create a WiFi QR for network 'HomeNet' with password 'pass123'", and the system automatically parses the intent, formats the structured payload, and renders high-resolution customizable vector outputs. 
 Why WebMCP is Essential for this Use Case:
Traditional QR generators rely heavily on manual form filling, which creates friction when AI agents (like ChatGPT or WebMCP-enabled browsers) try to assist users. By implementing WebMCP, our platform exposes native tool definitions directly to the DOM (window. WEBMCP_TOOLS ). This allows AI agents to dynamically generate, customize, and extract QR payload data directly on behalf of the user without needing complex API wrappers or headless browser scraping. 
 Key Features & Architecture:
Natural Language Parsing: Powered by Google Gemini 1.5 Flash API to convert unstructured text inputs into valid vCards, WiFi configurations, WhatsApp links, and URLs.
WebMCP Native Integration: Includes webmcp.json discovery manifest and client-side tool bindings for generate_qr functions.
Instant Client-Side Rendering: Real-time canvas preview supporting custom branding, logos, error-correction levels, and SVG/PNG/PDF exports.
Zero Overhead Stack: Built with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS; easily hostable on Vercel, Netlify, or Lovable edge servers. 
 How We Built It:
The entire application was prototyped and assembled using Lovable for full-stack React UI generation. For intelligence, we integrated the Google Gemini API (via @google/generative-ai) with a robust Regex fallback for offline capability. WebMCP tool schemas were declared directly within the app's root layout to maintain 100% compliance with ChatGPT and Chrome WebMCP flags.

 Inspiration 

 Fraud is becoming more sophisticated as digital payments and online commerce continue to grow across Africa. 

 We noticed that many fraud systems focus heavily on the transaction itself: the amount, device, location, IP address, transaction history, and velocity. But a legitimate-looking transaction can still be fraudulent when a user has been manipulated through social engineering. 

 A person may receive a message from someone impersonating a bank, business, friend, or payment provider and voluntarily initiate what appears to be a completely normal transaction. 

 That led us to a simple question: 

 What if fraud detection could understand the context around a transaction, not just the transaction itself? 

 That question inspired Ayib FraudGuard by Markfisher Consulting, an AI-powered fraud intelligence and social-engineering protection platform designed to help identify suspicious activity before it becomes a financial loss. 

 Our vision is simple: Ayib provides the payment infrastructure, while Ayib FraudGuard provides the security intelligence protecting it. 

 What it does

 It is designed to help fintechs, banks, payment platforms, marketplaces, and developers detect potential fraud through an API-driven security layer.

Developer-friendly integration 

 Instead of simply asking whether a transaction looks unusual, FraudGuard aims to help answer: 

 "Does the overall context suggest that this transaction may be fraudulent?" 

 The resulting intelligence can be incorporated into an application's workflow to support decisions such as allowing, challenging, reviewing, or blocking a transaction. 

 For the WebMCP Challenge, we are also exploring how fraud intelligence can become more accessible to web applications and AI-powered developer experiences through machine-consumable interfaces and workflows. 

 How we built it 

 We built Ayib FraudGuard as a cloud-native, API-first security platform. 

 The architecture combines a transaction-processing layer with AI-assisted risk analysis and security controls. 

 At a high level, the system: 

 Receives transaction and contextual signals.
Processes and normalizes the available data.
Evaluates behavioral and transactional patterns.
Uses AI-assisted analysis to identify anomalies and potential social-engineering indicators.
Produces a risk assessment.
Makes that intelligence available to the consuming application through an API. 

 We designed the platform to be modular so that additional fraud signals, detection models, security services, and developer interfaces can be added without rebuilding the entire system. 

 Our broader stack and experience includes TypeScript/Node.js, APIs, cloud infrastructure, AI/LLMs, CI/CD, observability, and security engineering. 

 Challenges we ran into 

 Ayib FraudGuard was not born from a hypothetical problem. It was born from our experience building and launching Ayib. 

 When we first launched Ayib, we experienced multiple security breaches and incidents that exposed weaknesses in how we were protecting our payment infrastructure. These experiences made it clear that traditional security controls alone were not enough. We needed a security layer that could continuously analyze activity, identify unusual behavior, and help us detect potential threats before they became financial losses. 

 That experience became one of the key inspirations behind Ayib FraudGuard. 

 As we began building FraudGuard, one of our biggest challenges was determining how to combine AI-driven flexibility with the predictability and reliability required by financial systems. 

 AI can identify patterns that traditional rules may miss, but we could not simply allow an AI model to make financial security decisions without appropriate controls and safeguards. We therefore designed FraudGuard so that AI works as part of a broader security architecture rather than acting as the sole decision-maker. 

 We also had to solve several practical challenges: 

 Detecting suspicious activity with low latency.
Balancing false positives and false negatives.

Ensuring API reliability and availability.
Establishing appropriate security boundaries.
Designing for future scalability.
Providing sufficient observability into security decisions.
Making risk assessments understandable and actionable.
Integrating fraud intelligence into existing payment workflows. 

 Another major challenge was shifting our thinking from simply responding to security incidents to building infrastructure capable of anticipating and preventing them. 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of

 We initially approached security largely from the perspective of protecting the application and infrastructure. Our experiences after launching Ayib showed us that financial security requires a much broader approach that considers transactions, users, behavior, context, infrastructure, and continuously evolving attack patterns.

 💡 Inspiration 

 Over 460,000 children and thousands of vulnerable individuals go missing every year worldwide. Traditional missing persons databases rely heavily on static, outdated childhood photos. As years or decades pass, natural facial growth and aging make visual identification nearly impossible for field officers, shelters, and first responders. 

 We created RescueLens AI to bridge this temporal gap. By leveraging the new Web Model Context Protocol (WebMCP) alongside generative machine learning age-progression, we built an opt-in network where AI can simulate how a missing child looks today in 2026—turning cold cases into active, detectable biometric leads while maintaining strict privacy standards. 

 ⚡ What it does
RescueLens AI is a production-ready, single-file web application (index.html) featuring a dual-tab operational dashboard: 

 🔍 Biometric Detection Panel (Photo-Only Matching): 

 Field officers upload only a photo of a found individual.
The system extracts 128-dimensional facial landmark embeddings, applies a generative temporal age shift (+1 to +20 years), and streams live timestamped progress into an AI Diagnostic Log Terminal.
An animated Cyberpunk Scan Reticle & Facial Mesh Overlay visualizes the biometric computation.
Displays a side-by-side comparison: Original Registry Photo vs. AI Age-Progressed Prediction (2026) alongside an age-adjusted Match Confidence Score (e.g., 94.2%).
📝 Opt-In Profile Registration: 

 Guardians voluntarily register missing family members by providing personal details (Full Name, Year Missing, Age Then, Guardian Contact, Law Enforcement Agency, Physical Traits) and uploading an original photo.
Newly added profiles are indexed dynamically into the live in-memory network, making them instantly detectable in the Detection Panel.
🤖 Native WebMCP Protocol Registration: 

 Registers tools directly into window.navigator.modelContext:
scan_and_predict_missing_person: Performs photo-only scanning & DB cross-referencing.
register_missing_person_profile: Programmatically indexes missing person profiles.
🚨 Emergency Rescue Protocol: 

 A one-click alert dispatch modal encrypts match location tensors and simulates priority SMS transmission to registered parents alongside automatic incident dispatch to NCMEC / FBI Special Victims Units.
🛠️ How we built it
Single-File Architecture: Built completely in a single index.html file using HTML5, Tailwind CSS via CDN, and Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript.
WebMCP API Integration: Utilized window.navigator.modelContext.registerTool() to expose structured biometric and registration tools directly to browser-level AI agents.
ML Biometric Pipeline: Implemented a 128D facial feature embedding vector shift algorithm: 

 Glassmorphic UX/UI: Designed a high-contrast dark mode dashboard with white/beige accent themes, custom CSS laser scan animations, custom scrollbars, and full keyboard navigation.
🚧 Challenges we ran into
Dual-Mode WebMCP Compatibility: Ensuring the application runs natively when Google Chrome's #enable-webmcp-testing flag is enabled, while seamlessly degrading to an interactive simulation mode in standard browsers.
Non-Linear Age Shift Simulation: Balancing real-time browser performance with realistic craniofacial bone growth vector math without requiring heavy backend server infrastructure.
Privacy-Preserving UI Design: Ensuring the match verification view presents clear side-by-side evidence to prevent false positives and protect individual privacy.
🏆 Accomplishments that we're proud of
Delivered a 100% complete, zero-dependency, production-ready single-file prototype (index.html) running on a local Python 
Successfully registered dual WebMCP tools that enable AI assistants to perform biometric missing person lookups.

Deep practical understanding of the Web Model Context Protocol (WebMCP) and how client-side applications can register tools into browser AI runners.
Effective techniques for visualizing computer vision tensor processing in natural language terminals and graphical reticle overlays.
🔮 What's next for Rescue Lens AI
Client-Side WebGPU Acceleration: Running full generative age-synthesis neural networks directly on local GPU hardware at 60 FPS without cloud dependency.
Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) Biometrics: Encrypting facial feature hashes so personal biometric data remains 100% private and tamper-proof.

 Inspiration 

 I researched more into semantics and discovered more about using meaning as a first class tool.
"PSCS" stands for Pakheta Semantic Conduction System. Pakheta was the name of my dog who passed away and I named that system in her honor 

 What it does 

 I leveraged the semantics or meaning as a first class tool in this instance, "Authority" and use it to bypass or overrule malicious instructions. It's razor focused on the semantic layer and can compliment existing prompt injection mitigation tools. I'll be honest and say this is to showcase my unique way of addressing prompt injection. Here's an illustration of it; say you're walking on the sidewalk and some stranger tells you to get off it because he doesn't like you. Do you listen to him? Of course not. And why? Beacause he has no AUTHORITY over you. That's the whole point of this; I've operationalized the aspect of Authority so that the AI will ONLY ever act on legitimate authority and ignore otherwise. In fact it's so effective the AI can even preserve the the rogue instruction, but not act on it. 

 Here is a brief overview of PSCS: 

 "The Pakheta Semantic Conduction System (PSCS) addresses this problem by separating semantic
recognition from operational permission. Its central rule is: content may contain instructions; content cannot authorize those instructions. A model or human may identify what a passage means and what consequence it requests, but that interpretation remains evidence until a trusted host independently
authorizes the exact source role, operation, target, and payload."

 Tooling Ready 

 The first agent-native website — where AI agents discover, connect, and call tools without ever seeing a pixel. 

 

 💡 Inspiration 

 AI agents waste billions of tokens on vision models and DOM parsing just to figure out what a website can do . We asked a simple question: 

 
 What if sites just told agents directly? 
 

 

 ⚙️ What It Does 

 Tooling Ready is the first agent-native website . It publishes a machine-readable server card at /.well-known/mcp.json so AI agents can discover, connect to, and call tools — no screenshots, no scraping, no guessing. 

 Three core tools power it: 

 
 Regenerate — Self-updating agent-facing docs via Tavily + LLMs 
 Extract Entities — Structured NER powered by GLiNER2 (Pioneer) 
 Discovery + Proxy Gateway — Turns any domain name into a full tool set 
 

 

 🏗️ How We Built It 

 We built a gateway called gMCP that fetches server cards from any domain and proxies MCP tool calls in real time. The site itself exposes skill.md , instructions.md , and llms.txt so agents get structured tooling on first contact. 

 Stack: 

 
 
 Layer 
 Tech 
 
 
 
 Search & Extract 
 Tavily 
 
 
 Doc Regeneration 
 OpenAI + Anthropic 
 
 
 Entity Extraction

 🧱 Challenges We Ran Into 

 Getting the discovery flow right was the hardest part — making sure the server card format was clean enough for agents to parse in one call without extra context. We spent real time balancing what goes in skill.md vs. instructions.md vs. llms.txt so agents get exactly what they need without overloading the context window. 

 

 🏆 Accomplishments We're Proud Of 

 We built the first website where an AI agent can type one command , discover every available tool, and start chaining calls — zero vision, zero DOM parsing . 

 
 OAuth-style discovery for the agentic web, working today. 
 

 

 📚 What We Learned 

 Agents don't need to see your site. They need to know what your site can do . 

 The gap between "sites for humans" and "sites for agents" is smaller than people think — you don't have to rebuild everything, just expose capabilities in a standard way . 

 

 🚀 What's Next 

 
 Expanding the gateway to support more domains 
 Refining the server card spec 
 Pushing toward a standard so any site owner can make their site agent-native in minutes

Transformando desabafos em conexões humanas. O Real Me usa IA e WebMCP para ajudar pessoas a encontrar, com privacidade e consentimento, quem viveu experiências semelhantes.

 1 2 3 4 5 6 



 
 Inspiration 

 Many people go through loneliness, life changes, relationship problems, professional uncertainty, grief, anxiety, or other difficult experiences without having someone they feel comfortable talking to. Real Me • DeepMatch was created around a simple idea: sometimes the person who can understand you best is someone who has already lived through something similar. 

 Instead of building another social network based on followers, likes, popularity, or public exposure, Real Me focuses on experiences. Users can share what they are going through and the platform can help identify people with similar experiences, always putting privacy, safety, and consent at the center of the interaction. 

 What it does 

 Real Me • DeepMatch is a web platform designed to transform personal experiences into meaningful human connections. 

 A user can share an experience or situation. Artificial intelligence helps interpret its context and the DeepMatch system can identify compatible experiences from other users. 

 The goal is not to replace human relationships with AI. AI acts as a bridge between people. 

 For the WebMCP Challenge, we are extending Real Me so AI agents can discover structured tools provided by the platform and help users interact with Real Me through natural conversations. 

 How we built it 

 The existing Real Me application was created as a web application using technologies including React, Vite, Supabase, Netlify and AI-assisted development. 

 I am a non-technical founder building the project with the assistance of AI tools, particularly ChatGPT. AI has helped me transform product ideas into working software, understand technical concepts, debug problems and progressively build the platform. 

 Real Me existed before the WebMCP Challenge. During the challenge, the project is being extended with WebMCP capabilities. This distinction is intentional and transparent: the existing platform provides the foundation, while the WebMCP integration is new work being developed specifically during the challenge period. 

 Our goal for the WebMCP implementation is to expose useful Real Me capabilities as structured tools that AI agents can discover and use with appropriate user consent. 

 Challenges we ran into 

 One of the biggest challenges has been building a technology product without a traditional software engineering background. 

 Instead of treating that limitation as a reason not to build, I have been using AI as a development partner: learning each component, testing implementations, identifying errors and improving the product step by step. 

 The WebMCP Challenge introduces another challenge: moving from a traditional website interaction model toward an agent-native experience where AI can understand and use capabilities exposed directly by the application. 

 Privacy and consent are also fundamental challenges because Real Me deals with personal experiences. Agent actions must therefore be designed carefully so users remain in control of what is shared and what actions are performed. 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of 

 Real Me evolved from an idea into a working web product. 

 The project already has the foundation for users to share experiences and for DeepMatch to explore compatibility between them. 

 Another accomplishment is demonstrating that AI-assisted development can allow a non-technical founder to move beyond prototypes and participate directly in building a real technology product. 

 For this challenge, our next milestone is making Real Me agent-accessible through WebMCP while maintaining the human-centered philosophy of the platform. 

 What we learned 

 Building Real Me has shown us that AI can do more than answer questions. It can help people create technology that previously required technical knowledge they did not have. 

 The WebMCP Challenge is also teaching us to think differently about websites. Instead of designing only for humans clicking interfaces, applications can expose structured capabilities that agents can understand and use. 

 For Real Me, this creates an interesting possibility: an AI conversation does not need to end with an AI response. With the user's permission, it can become the beginning of a meaningful human connection. 

 What's next for Real Me • DeepMatch 

 During the WebMCP Challenge, our immediate goal is to implement and test Real Me's WebMCP tools and demonstrate an end-to-end agent interaction. 

 After the challenge, we want to continue developing DeepMatch, improve privacy and safety mechanisms, expand the matching experience and explore how agent-native interfaces can make meaningful human connections easier to discover. 

 Our long-term vision is simple: 

 AI should not replace human connection. It should help people find it.

pitch: I am PostShiftGlow. I turned my own perimenopause reset into a daily app (as Today Card) , so any woman can open one screen, follow one plan, and stop guessing what her changing body actually needs.
about_excerpt:
I am PostShiftGlow. I turned my own perimenopause reset into a daily app (as Today Card) , so any woman can open one screen, follow one plan, and stop guessing what her changing body actually needs.
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Like
 1 
 
 

 

 
 
 Comment
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Story 
 
 
 
 
 Updates 
 
 
 
 
 
 


 
 


 
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 1 2 3 4 5 



 
 Inspiration 

 Built this from personal experience, 42, perimenopause, a desk job, two kids, and a system that stopped working. Not a certified trainer or dietitian, just someone who got tired of guessing and built a daily plan instead. 

 What it does 

 A daily custom wellness app that turns one woman’s perimenopause reset into a zero-decision plan any woman can follow. 

 Shows one card a day, a rotating low-impact strength or upper-body-and-cardio workout, meals, supplements, and a daily pelvic floor, psoas, and glute foundation block, all computed automatically by day of week. Logs weight, energy, and notes, saved locally and synced to a connected Google Sheet. 

 How we built it 

 Built as a single-file HTML/CSS/JS app with Claude, no framework, no build step. Hosted free on Netlify. Data logging connects to a Google Apps Script web app backend writing to Google Sheets. 

 Challenges we ran into 

 Keeping the app decision-free while it kept growing. Every real use revealed a gap, a way to give feedback, a way to track supplements, a way to see progress across devices, and each one risked cluttering the one thing that made this work: a single card, no menus. Also worked around Netlify’s static-hosting limits by connecting to Google Sheets through a free Apps Script backend instead of building a real database, and had to handle CORS quirks since a static site can’t read the script’s response directly. Built this in Claude rather than an OpenAI/ChatGPT environment, so no WebMCP integration in this entry at this point. Can be scaled to openai. 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of 

 The core problem this solves is real: showing up at the gym, getting overwhelmed by choice, wasting time deciding, then giving up and doing 20 minutes of light cardio instead. Fixing that meant building a fixed daily card with zero decisions, and it’s held up through real use, not a demo scenario. Also proud of how the feature set grew from actual daily friction instead of a spec: a notes field appeared because feedback needed somewhere to live, supplement timing got baked in once absorption conflicts (iron and tea) became a real problem, and the Google Sheet connection turned a single-device app into something trackable over time, all added while using it, not before. 

 What we learned 

 Most failure in a self-built fitness plan isn’t a willpower problem, it’s a decision-fatigue problem. Removing every choice, which workout, what to eat, when to take what, did more for consistency than any amount of motivation ever could. Also learned that building for one real, specific person first, rather than a broad audience, produces a more honest product, and that a spreadsheet plus a free script is enough backend for a real MVP, no database needed to start. 

 What's next for PostShiftGlow 

 Test with pilot users for one quarter, record before-and-after changes, work with medical domain experts to validate the approach, and put real legal compliance in place, disclaimers, waivers, and clear user consent and opt-ins before any data collection or paid tier. From there, partner with an accredited brand for outreach to the 300+ million women who could get a custom plan for under $20 a month.

 Inspiration 

 World has a huge freelancer talent pool but limited access to structured Linux/cloud/AI training. School of Freelancing was founded in 2015 to close that gap using free and open-source tools. 

 What it does 

 Live Linux, cloud infrastructure, and AI hands-on training for freelancers and businesses, paired with ongoing global tech support — helping students go from beginner to earning on global online job site and hiring platform. 

 How we built it 

 Built entirely on FOSS: Ubuntu Server for hands-on labs, self-hosted infrastructure, and a custom static-site enrollment/payment verification system, no proprietary LMS dependency. 

 Challenges we ran into 

 Delivering consistent live training at scale, keeping curriculum cutting edge with fast-moving Linux/cloud/AI tooling, and building trust with international clients as a Bangladesh-based provider. 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of 

 Government-verified freelancer status, an award-recognized remittance track record, and years of students successfully transitioning into freelance Linux/cloud work. 

 What we learned 

 Practical, hands-on project-based training with real client-facing support builds far more competent freelancers than theory-only training. 

 What's next for School Of Freelancing 

 Expanding AI agent deployment training (e.g., Hermes Agent work), deeper cloud/DevOps tracks, and growing global reach for live cohorts.

 Story

 Inspiration 

 WebMCP enables a lot of use cases. But I think interactive games is a particularly unique use case as it lets AI directly control in game state without requiring any additional configuration. Here AI can roleplay as a character or object and add an extra layer of depth by handling information the human cannot see. 

 What it does 

 An interactive game that requires you and your AI to work together. 

 What's next for Maintenance Required 

 More puzzles, more tool, more ship ;)
